audit_items.proof_trace: The CorrectSubnet validation uses strings.Contains() for substring matching instead of exact subnet ID comparison. This allows column index 1 to pass validation on subnets 10-19, 21, 31, 41, etc., because the check verifies if '/data_column_sidecar_10/' contains '/data_column_sidecar_1/', which succeeds due to substring '1' in '10'. The trailing slash mitigation (line 148) only prevents the reverse case.
audit_items.attack_scenario: Attacker broadcasts data column sidecar with index=1 (correct subnet=1) on wrong subnets 10, 11, 12, 100, 110, etc. The strings.Contains check at line 153 accepts these because '10', '11', '12', '100', '110' all contain substring '1', violating the spec requirement that compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar(index) must equal subnet_id.
